te: First... who actually says no to you at the hospital desk?
en: First... who actually says no to you at the hospital desk?

te: Most people think it's the insurance company sitting there evaluating your medical reports.
en: Most people think it's the insurance company sitting there evaluating your medical reports.

te: But in reality, it's a middleman called a T-P-A...
en: But in reality, it's a middleman called a T-P-A...

te: Third Party Administrator.
en: Third Party Administrator.

te: Many think a T-P-A is a neutral government doctor.
en: Many think a T-P-A is a neutral government doctor.

te: It is not.
en: It is not.

te: A T-P-A is a company hired and paid by the insurance company to process medical bills.
en: A T-P-A is a company hired and paid by the insurance company to process medical bills.

te: In India, about seven out of every ten health claims are settled through T-P-As.
en: In India, about seven out of every ten health claims are settled through T-P-As.

te: Under I-R-D-A-I rules, no claim can be rejected without the approval of the insurance company's own claims review committee.
en: Under I-R-D-A-I rules, no claim can be rejected without the approval of the insurance company's own claims review committee.

te: But here are the three excuses you will often see on these letters.
en: But here are the three excuses you will often see on these letters.

te: Excuse Number One.
en: Excuse Number One.

te: Non-disclosure of pre-existing condition.
en: Non-disclosure of pre-existing condition.

te: Suppose you were admitted for a broken leg or dengue.
en: Suppose you were admitted for a broken leg or dengue.

te: A junior doctor writes one line in your notes.
en: A junior doctor writes one line in your notes.

te: Patient has mild blood pressure.
en: Patient has mild blood pressure.

te: The reviewer sees that one line.
en: The reviewer sees that one line.

te: He opens your proposal form from five years ago, and says...
en: He opens your proposal form from five years ago, and says...

te: You didn't declare blood pressure.
en: You didn't declare blood pressure.

te: Cashless denied.
en: Cashless denied.

te: Wait... does blood pressure cause a broken leg or a dengue infection?
en: Wait... does blood pressure cause a broken leg or a dengue infection?

te: Of course not.
en: Of course not.

te: But in the first five years of your policy, the company can still use it.
en: But in the first five years of your policy, the company can still use it.

te: After five years, the rule changes.
en: After five years, the rule changes.

te: Excuse Number Two.
en: Excuse Number Two.

te: Not medically necessary.
en: Not medically necessary.

te: They say your treatment could have been done as an outpatient visit without staying in hospital.
en: They say your treatment could have been done as an outpatient visit without staying in hospital.

te: And Excuse Number Three.
en: And Excuse Number Three.

te: Room rent limit, and proportionate deduction.
en: Room rent limit, and proportionate deduction.

te: Say your policy allows a room of five thousand rupees a day, but you took an eight thousand rupee room.
en: Say your policy allows a room of five thousand rupees a day, but you took an eight thousand rupee room.

te: They don't just deduct the three thousand rupee difference.
en: They don't just deduct the three thousand rupee difference.

te: They pay only five out of every eight rupees... on the surgery, doctor, and nursing charges too.
en: They pay only five out of every eight rupees... on the surgery, doctor, and nursing charges too.

te: That is a cut of about thirty-seven percent on those charges.
en: That is a cut of about thirty-seven percent on those charges.

te: When a family sees that technical rejection letter, they feel completely helpless.
en: When a family sees that technical rejection letter, they feel completely helpless.

te: They think the door is closed forever.
en: They think the door is closed forever.

te: It is not.
en: It is not.

te: A cashless denial... is NOT a claim rejection.
en: A cashless denial... is NOT a claim rejection.

te: Your legal right to the money is still alive.
en: Your legal right to the money is still alive.
